company.name: Albion Apron Services Ltd
company.description: Licensed airport ground handling and airside transport operator based at London Heathrow (IATA LHR / ICAO EGLL) with a GSE pool depot on the Eastern Apron between Terminal 2 and Terminal 4, plus a satellite team at Manchester Airport (MAN / EGCC). Core services: ramp handling with conventional and towbarless aircraft pushback tugs, baggage belt loaders, container/pallet high loaders for ULDs, self-propelled passenger steps for remote stands, low-floor apron passenger buses (Cobus) for terminal-to-aircraft transfers, and Type I/IV de-icing/anti-icing in the winter season. Every unit is a GSE asset with airside GPS positioning, OBD2/CAN telematics and utility-box telemetry (engine hours, hydraulic pressure, anti-collision proximity sensing, de-icing tank level and fluid temperature). Tasking is flight-linked per turnaround (flight number, gate/stand, STA/STD, ATA/ATD, on-block/off-block). Operated under UK aviation security (CAA / airport security programme) with airside passes, Airside Driving Permits (ADP) and Aircraft Driving Authorisation (RTADA), ADR/Carriage of Dangerous Goods for de-icing fluid and fuelling-adjacent logistics, DVSA MOT and operator (O) licence for road-registered shuttle and service vehicles, DVLA registration and EU/GB tachograph & drivers hours for shuttle drivers. Road-registered vehicles carry UK number plates and MOT records; pure airside GSE carry internal fleet numbers and airside identifiers instead of road plates.

notes.author: James Whitmore
notes.body: Pushback BX221 from stand 233 went smoothly. Headset comms clear with flight deck, towbar disconnected, bypass pin removed and shown to crew, all-clear hand signal given. Off-block on time at 05:58.

notes.author: James Whitmore
notes.body: Towbarless push of CS884 B777F from widebody stand 545. Nose-gear cradle engaged correctly, overload monitor green throughout. Released cleanly on taxiway Bravo. Crew thanked ground.

notes.author: Priya Raghunathan
notes.body: Full ULD load on CS885. 24 PMC main deck plus 14 AKE lower deck. High loader platform a touch slow to raise on first cycle, hydraulic pressure recovered after warm-up. Loadmaster signed off all locks.

notes.author: Priya Raghunathan
notes.body: Anti-collision auto-slow triggered approaching the fuselage on stand 553. Recommend logging the proximity sensor sensitivity for review, it cut in earlier than expected but operation was safe.

notes.author: Connor MacLeod
notes.body: Remote stand 210 boarding for MH412. Three Cobus trips, steps at door 1L. One passenger required assistance, ambulift not needed. All pax cleared by 14:35.

notes.author: Connor MacLeod
notes.body: Brief geofence alert when I lined up near the taxiway holding area on the apron roadway. I held short and reversed clear once I realised the painted line. No conflict with any aircraft.

notes.author: Fleet Engineering
notes.body: Tug 110 withdrawn after a hydraulic seep was spotted at the steering ram during the daily walkaround. Unit is AOG. Cover provided by PB-101. Seal kit ordered, ETA 26 June.

notes.author: Aisha Okonkwo
notes.body: Summer readiness check on de-icer 707. Boom articulation full range, nozzle spray pattern even, heat exchanger holding 60 C. Type IV refractometer reading within spec. Unit kept serviceable for any out-of-season frost call.

notes.author: Aisha Okonkwo
notes.body: ADR tank periodic inspection falls due by 15 July. Flagged to workshop so the de-icer is not committed to a job around that date. Placards stowed correctly for the empty repositioning move.

notes.author: Megan Pritchard
notes.body: Early crew shuttle, 14 aboard from the staff hub. Tacho card in, drivers hours fine for the shift. Cleared the vehicle search at Control Post East without issue. Dropped crew at the GSE pool.

notes.author: Sophie Bennett
notes.body: Pier A airbridge faulted so we ran four Cobus trips for PS501 instead of using the bridge. 162 pax moved without delay to the flight. Manchester apron control kept us updated on the roadway.

notes.author: Operations Control
notes.body: Reminder issued to Priya that her Airside Driving Permit (ADP-R) is due for renewal by 15 September. Refresher and assessment to be booked in August to avoid a lapse.

notes.author: Fleet Engineering
notes.body: PB-110 on jacks in bay 3. Old steering ram seals perished, new seal kit due 26 June. Plan to pressure-test and release the tug back to the pool the same afternoon if the kit arrives on time.
